Gods of knowledge vary from masters of arcane magic to patrons of craft and invention. To them, knowledge is more valuable than material wealth, and the desire to learn is an act of worship. Libraries, universities, and other institutions dedicated to education also draw on the power of the Knowledge Domain.

On Faerûn, Clerics of the Knowledge Domain worship deities of learning and ingenuity like Oghma and Gond. Other powerful deities—such as Asmodeus, Mystra, Savras, and Jergal—also count Clerics of the Knowledge Domain among their devotees, as do less-common divinities like Deneir, the Scribe of Oghma, and Azuth, servant of Mystra.

Source:	Unearthed Arcana: Forgotten Realms Subclasses p. 2

feature.name: Level 3: Blessings of Knowledge (Knowledge Domain (UA))
feature.text:
You gain proficiency with one type of Artisan's Tools of your choice and in two of the following skills of your choice: Arcana, History, Nature, or Religion. You have Expertise in those two skills.

Source:	Unearthed Arcana: Forgotten Realms Subclasses p. 2

feature.name: Level 3: Knowledge Domain Spells (Knowledge Domain (UA))
feature.text:
When you reach a Cleric level specified in the Knowledge Domain Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

Knowledge Domain Spells:
Level | Spells
3 | Command, Comprehend Languages, Detect Magic, Detect Thoughts, Identify, Mind Spike
5 | Dispel Magic, Nondetection, Tongues
7 | Arcane Eye, Banishment, Confusion
9 | Legend Lore, Scrying, Synaptic Static

Source:	Unearthed Arcana: Forgotten Realms Subclasses p. 2

feature.name: Level 3: Mind Magic (Knowledge Domain (UA))
feature.text:
As a Magic action, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity to manifest your magical knowledge. Choose one spell from the Knowledge Domain Spells table that you have prepared. As part of that action, you cast that spell without expending a spell slot or needing Material components.

Source:	Unearthed Arcana: Forgotten Realms Subclasses p. 3

feature.name: Level 6: Unfettered Mind (Knowledge Domain (UA))
feature.text:
You gain telepathy out to 60 feet. When you use this telepathy, you can simultaneously contact a number of creatures equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of one).

Additionally, if your total for an Intelligence check is lower than your Wisdom score, you can use that score in place of the total.

Source:	Unearthed Arcana: Forgotten Realms Subclasses p. 3

feature.name: Level 17: Divine Foreknowledge (Knowledge Domain (UA))
feature.text:
As a Bonus Action, you magically expand your mind to the possibilities of the future. For 1 hour, you have Advantage on D20 Tests. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest. You can also restore your use of this feature by expending a level 6+ spell slot (no action required).

Source:	Unearthed Arcana: Forgotten Realms Subclasses p. 3

feature.name: Cleric Subclass: Grave Domain (UA)
feature.text:
Embody Deific Forces of Death

The Grave Domain concerns itself with the boundary between life and death. To those who tap into this domain's power, death is a foundational, natural, and inevitable part of the multiverse. Such Clerics seek to destroy Undead and strive to shepherd spirits to the afterlife (whether those spirits want to go or not).
	The magic of this domain also allows these Clerics to stave off death for a time, particularly for those who still have some great work to accomplish in the world. But this is merely a delay of death, not a denial of it, for the grave will always claim its due.

Design Note: Grave Domain Updates
Here are the main updates in this subclass since its appearance in Xanathar's Guide to Everything:

	• Circle of Mortality now also grants you a small damage boost against Bloodied creatures.

	• Grave Domain Spells has been updated to include more versatility and combat-relevant spells.

	• Path to the Grave now produces an ongoing curse effect in addition to boosting the damage of an attack.

	• Sentinel at Death's Door now can trigger on any attack, not just Critical Hits.

	• Divine Reaper is a new feature that absorbs the previous benefits of Keeper of Souls and provides a boost to the Cleric's Necromancy spells.

Source:	UA2024-Horror Subclasses p. 4

feature.name: Level 3: Circle of Mortality (Grave Domain (UA))
feature.text:
You gain the ability to manipulate the balance between life and death, granting you the following benefits.

	Pull of Death. Once per turn, when you cast a spell or hit with an attack roll and deal damage to a Bloodied creature, that creature takes an extra 1d4 Necrotic damage.

	Return to Life. When you would normally roll one or more dice to restore Hit Points to a creature at 0 Hit Points with a spell or Channel Divinity, don't roll those dice for the healing; instead use the highest number possible for each die. For example, instead of restoring 2d4 Hit Points to a creature at 0 Hit Points with a spell, you restore 8.

Source:	UA2024-Horror Subclasses p. 4

feature.name: Level 3: Grave Domain Spells (Grave Domain (UA))
feature.text:
Your connection to this divine domain ensures you always have certain spells ready. When you reach a Cleric level specified in the Grave Domain Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

Grave Domain Spells:
Cleric Level | Spells
3 | Bane, Chill Touch, Detect Evil and Good, Gentle Repose, Ray of Enfeeblement
5 | Revivify, Vampiric Touch
7 | Blight, Dispel Evil and Good
9 | Hold Monster, Raise Dead

Source:	UA2024-Horror Subclasses p. 4

feature.name: Level 3: Path To the Grave (Grave Domain (UA))
feature.text:
As a Bonus Action, you present your Holy Symbol and expend a use of your Channel Divinity to curse one creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself until the start of your next turn. While cursed, the creature has Disadvantage on attack rolls and saving throws.
	When you or an ally you can see hits the cursed target with an attack roll, you can end the curse early (no action required) to make the attack deal extra Necrotic or Radiant damage (your choice) equal to 1d8 plus your Cleric level.

Source:	UA2024-Horror Subclasses p. 5

feature.name: Level 6: Sentinel At Death's Door (Grave Domain (UA))
feature.text:
When you or a Bloodied creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself is hit with an attack roll, you can take a Reaction to halve that attack's damage.
	You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	UA2024-Horror Subclasses p. 5

feature.name: Level 17: Divine Reaper (Grave Domain (UA))
feature.text:
Your deep connection to this domain renders you a hallowed harbinger of death, granting you the following benefits.

	Enhanced Necromancy. When you cast a spell of level 5 or lower from the Necromancy school that targets one creature or a spell from the Grave Domain Spells table, you can expend a use of Channel Divinity to target a second creature within the spell's range. If the spell requires costly or consumed Material components, you must provide Material components for each target.

	Keeper of Souls. When an enemy dies within 60 feet of you, you or one creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself regains Hit Points equal to three times your Cleric level. You can't use this feature if you have the Incapacitated condition. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

Source:	UA2024-Horror Subclasses p. 5

feature.name: Cleric Subclass: Arcana Domain (UA)
feature.text:
Blend Conviction with Arcane Power

Magic suffuses the multiverse and fuels both destruction and creation. Clerics with this domain view magical knowledge not as power to be used in pursuit of personal ends, but as a gift they have the responsibility to share.
	Gods associated with the Arcana Domain know the secrets and potential of magic intimately. These gods are often connected to knowledge, as learning and arcane power tend to go hand-in-hand, or to secrecy or power.

Source:	UA25-ArcaneSubclasses p. 1

feature.name: Level 3: Arcana Domain Spells (Arcana Domain (UA))
feature.text:
Your connection to this divine domain means you always have certain spells ready. When you reach a Cleric level specified in the Arcana Domain Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

Arcana Domain Spells:
Cleric Level | Prepared Spells
3 | Detect Magic, Magic Missile, Magic Weapon, Nystul's Magic Aura
5 | Counterspell, Dispel Magic
7 | Arcane Eye, Leomund's Secret Chest
9 | Bigby's Hand, Teleportation Circle

Source:	UA25-ArcaneSubclasses p. 1

feature.name: Level 3: Arcane Initiate (Arcana Domain (UA))
feature.text:
You gain the following benefits.

	Arcane Knowledge. You gain proficiency in the Arcana skill if you don't have it already. You also gain Expertise in the Arcana skill.

	Cantrips. You learn two Wizard cantrips of your choice. Whenever you gain a Cleric level, you can replace one of these cantrips with another Wizard cantrip.

Source:	UA25-ArcaneSubclasses p. 2

feature.name: Level 3: Modify Magic (Arcana Domain (UA))
feature.text:
You can use your Channel Divinity to alter your spells as you cast them. When you cast a spell, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity and change the spell in one of the following ways (no action required).

	Fortifying Spell. One target of the spell gains a number of Temporary Hit Points equal to 2d8 plus your Cleric level.

	Tenacious Spell. When you cast a spell that forces a creature to make a saving throw, choose one target of the spell you can see. Roll 1d6 and apply the number rolled as a penalty to the target's saving throw.

Source:	UA25-ArcaneSubclasses p. 2

feature.name: Level 6: Dispelling Recovery (Arcana Domain (UA))
feature.text:
Immediately after you cast a spell with a spell slot that restores Hit Points to a creature or ends a condition on a creature, you can cast Dispel Magic on the creature as a Bonus Action without expending a spell slot.
	You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	UA25-ArcaneSubclasses p. 2

feature.name: Level 17: Arcane Mastery (Arcana Domain (UA))
feature.text:
You learn four Wizard spells, one from each of levels 6, 7, 8, and 9. You thereafter always have those spells prepared. Whenever you gain a Cleric level, you can replace one of these spells with another Wizard spell of the same level.

Source:	UA25-ArcaneSubclasses p. 2

feature.name: Cleric Subclass: Pestilence Domain (UA)
feature.text:
Foment Plague and Rot

Clerics of the Pestilence Domain harness supernatural plague and decay to erode their enemies' vitality. Though common folk often regard pestilence as a force of rampant destruction, Clerics of this domain wield it with surgical precision.
	The Pestilence Domain is associated with gods of poison, disease, famine, and rot. These deities use blighted crops, magical outbreaks, and swarms of insects and vermin to motivate or punish mortals in accordance with their doctrines. Their followers include apothecaries, doctors, poisoners, and royal tasters. Other followers might devote themselves to a god of pestilence to spare their communities or loved ones from plague.

Source:	Villainous Options p. 1 (Unearthed Arcana)

feature.name: Level 3: Blight Weaver (Pestilence Domain (UA))
feature.text:
You gain the following benefits.

	Inoculated Soul. You have Resistance to Necrotic and Poison damage, and you can't be infected by magical contagions.

	Rot and Fester. Damage from your Cleric spells and Cleric features ignores Resistance to Necrotic and Poison damage. Additionally, when you cast a Cleric spell or use a Cleric feature that deals either Necrotic or Poison damage, you can change that damage to the other type.

Source:	Villainous Options p. 1 (Unearthed Arcana)

feature.name: Level 3: Pestilence Domain Spells (Pestilence Domain (UA))
feature.text:
Your connection to this divine domain ensures you always have certain spells ready. When you reach a Cleric level specified in the Pestilence Domain Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

Pestilence Domain Spells:
Cleric Level | Prepared Spells
3 | Detect Poison and Disease, Protection from Poison, Ray of Enfeeblement, Ray of Sickness
5 | Stinking Cloud, Vampiric Touch
7 | Blight, Giant Insect
9 | Contagion, Insect Plague

Source:	Villainous Options p. 1 (Unearthed Arcana)

feature.name: Level 3: Plague Blessing (Pestilence Domain (UA))
feature.text:
As a Magic action, you can present your Holy Symbol and expend a use of Channel Divinity to manifest a 5-foot Emanation of withering plague that surrounds you or one willing creature you touch for 1 minute. It ends early if you dismiss it (no action required), manifest it again, or have the Incapacitated condition.
	Each creature of your choice that starts its turn in the Emanation must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC or gain 1 Exhaustion level. This feature can't increase a creature's Exhaustion level higher than a level equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1 Exhaustion level). For example, if you have a Wisdom score of 16, this feature can't increase a creature's Exhaustion level higher than 3.
	The plague spread by this feature manifests with a specific symptom. Choose it from the Plague Symptoms table or determine it randomly.

Plague Symptoms:
1d6 |  While Infected, a Creature ...
1 | Is drained of all color, appearing in monochromatic grays.
2 | Sheds metallic, rust-hued flakes and creaks while moving.
3 | Secretes foul-smelling mucus.
4 | Is surrounded by a cloud of buzzing insects.
5 | Sprouts fungi or other foliage from its flesh.
6 | Is covered in glowing pustules.

Source:	Villainous Options p. 2 (Unearthed Arcana)

feature.name: Level 6: Virulent Burst (Pestilence Domain (UA))
feature.text:
When an enemy within 60 feet of you is reduced to 0 Hit Points, you can take a Reaction to cause plague to burst from that creature, spreading pestilence in a 10-foot Emanation originating from the enemy; if the enemy had at least 1 Exhaustion level, the size of the Emanation increases to 20 feet.
	Each creature of your choice in the Emanation makes a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, a target suffers one of the following effects:

	Putrid Shock. The target has the Incapacitated condition until the end of its next turn. While Incapacitated, the target's Speed is 0.

	Toxic Infection. The target takes 3d6 Necrotic or Poison damage (your choice).

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	Villainous Options p. 2 (Unearthed Arcana)

feature.name: Level 17: Vermin Form (Pestilence Domain (UA))
feature.text:
As a Bonus Action, you can shape-shift into a Medium swarm of Tiny pests, such as cockroaches, maggots, or rats. While you're in this form, you retain your general shape, personality, memories, and the ability to speak; any equipment you're wearing or carrying doesn't transform with you, but you can continue using that equipment while in this form. Your game statistics remain the same, apart from the following changes:

	Condition Immunities. You have Immunity to the Grappled, Paralyzed, Prone, and Restrained conditions.

	Damage Resistances. You have Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage.

	Movement. You can enter and occupy another creature's space and vice versa. Additionally, you have a Climb Speed equal to your Speed, and you can climb difficult surfaces—including along ceilings—without needing to make an ability check.

	Plague Bites. Whenever you enter an enemy's space, that creature takes damage equal to your Wisdom modifier; the damage is Necrotic, Piercing, or Poison (your choice). A creature also takes this damage when it enters your space or ends its turn there. A creature takes this damage only once per turn.

You revert to your true form after 10 minutes, if you choose to end the transformation (no action required), if you have the Incapacitated condition, or if you die.
	Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest unless you expend a level 5+ spell slot (no action required) to restore your use of it.

Source:	Villainous Options p. 2 (Unearthed Arcana)

wizard.name: Wizard [5.5e]
wizard.proficiency: Intelligence, Wisdom, Arcana, History, Insight, Investigation, Medicine, Nature, Religion

trait.name: Wizard
trait.text:
Wizards are defined by their exhaustive study of magic's inner workings. They cast spells of explosive fire, arcing lightning, subtle deception, and spectacular transformations. Their magic conjures monsters from other planes of existence, glimpses the future, or forms protective barriers. Their mightiest spells change one substance into another, call meteors from the sky, or open portals to other worlds.
	Most Wizards share a scholarly approach to magic. They examine the theoretical underpinnings of magic, particularly the categorization of spells into schools of magic. Renowned Wizards such as Bigby, Tasha, Mordenkainen, and Yolande have built on their studies to invent iconic spells now used across the multiverse.
	The closest a Wizard is likely to come to an ordinary life is working as a sage or lecturer. Other Wizards sell their services as advisers, serve in military forces, or pursue lives of crime or domination.
	But the lure of knowledge calls even the most unadventurous Wizards from the safety of their libraries and laboratories and into crumbling ruins and lost cities. Most Wizards believe that their counterparts in ancient civilizations knew secrets of magic that have been lost to the ages, and discovering those secrets could unlock the path to a power greater than any magic available in the present age.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 165

feature.name: Becoming A Wizard As A Level 1 Character
feature.text:
As a 1st-level Wizard, you begin play with 6 + your Constitution modifier hit points.

Core Wizard Traits
Primary Ability: Intelligence
Hit Point Die: D6 per Wizard level
Saving Throw Proficiencies: Intelligence and Wisdom
Skill Proficiencies: Choose 2: Arcana, History, Insight, Investigation, Medicine, Nature, or Religion
Weapon Proficiencies: Simple weapons
Armor Training: None
Starting Equipment: Choose A or B: (A) 2 Daggers, Arcane Focus (Quarterstaff), Robe, Spellbook, Scholar's Pack, and 5 GP; or (B) 55 GP

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 165

feature.name: Becoming A Wizard As A Multiclass Character
feature.text:
Core Wizard Traits
Primary Ability: Intelligence
Hit Point Die: D6 per Wizard level

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 165

feature.name: Level 1: Spellcasting
feature.text:
As a student of arcane magic, you have learned to cast spells. See chapter 7 for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Wizard spells, which appear in the Wizard spell list later in the class's description.

	Cantrips. You know three Wizard cantrips of your choice. Light, Mage Hand, and Ray of Frost are recommended. Whenever you finish a Long Rest. you can replace one of your can trips from this feature with another Wizard cantrip of your choice.
	When you reach Wizard levels 4 and 10, you learn another Wizard cant rip of your choice, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Wizard Features table.

	Spellbook. Your wizardly apprenticeship culminated in the creation of a unique book: your spellbook. It is a Tiny object that weighs 3 pounds. contains 100 pages, and can be read only by you or someone casting Identify. You determine the book's appearance and materials, such as a gilt-edged tome or a collection of vellum bound with twine.
	The book contains the level 1+ spells you know. It starts with six level 1 Wizard spells of your choice. Detect Magic, Feather Fall, Mage Armor, Magic Missile. Sleep, and Thunderwave are recommended.
	Whenever you gain a Wizard level after 1, add two Wizard spells of your choice to your spell book. Each of these spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots, as shown in the Wizard Features table. The spells are the culmination of arcane research you do regularly.

	Spell Slots. The Wizard Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a Long Rest.

	Prepared Spells of Level 1+. You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To do so, choose four spells from your spellbook. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.
	The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Wizard levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Wizard Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional Wizard spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you're a level 3 Wizard, your list of prepared spells can include six spells of levels 1 and 2 in any combination, chosen from your spellbook.
	If another Wizard feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Wizard spells for you.

	Changing Your Prepared Spells. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change your list of prepared spells, replacing any of the spells there with spells from your spellbook.

	Spellcasting Ability. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your Wizard spells.

	Spellcasting Focus. You can use an Arcane Focus or your spellbook as a Spellcasting Focus for your Wizard spells.

Prepared Spells:
Level | Prepared Spells
1 | 4
2 | 5
3 | 6
4 | 7
5 | 9
6 | 10
7 | 11
8 | 12
9 | 14
10 | 15
11 | 16
12 | 16
13 | 17
14 | 18
15 | 19
16 | 21
17 | 22
18 | 23
19 | 24
20 | 25

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 165

feature.name: Expanding And Replacing A Spellbook
feature.text:
The spells you add to your spellbook as you gain levels reflect your ongoing magical research, but you might find other spells during your adventures that you can add to the book. You could discover a Wizard spell on a Spell Scroll, for example, and then copy it into your spellbook.

	Copying a Spell into the Book. When you find a level 1+ Wizard spell, you can copy it into your spellbook if it's of a level you can prepare and if you have time to copy it. For each level of the spell, the transcription takes 2 hours and costs 50 GP. Afterward you can prepare the spell like the other spells in your spellbook.

	Copying the Book. You can copy a spell from your spellbook into another book. This is like copying a new spell into your spellbook but faster, since you already know how to cast the spell. You need spend only 1 hour and 10 GP for each level of the copied spell.
	If you lose your spell book, you can use the same procedure to transcribe the Wizard spells that you have prepared into a new spellbook. Filling out the remainder of the new book requires you to find new spells to do so. For this reason, many wizards keep a backup spellbook.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 166

feature.name: Level 1: Ritual Adept
feature.text:
You can cast any spell as a Ritual if that spell has the Ritual tag and the spell is in your spellbook. You needn't have the spell prepared, but you must read from the book to cast a spell in this way.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 166

feature.name: Level 1: Arcane Recovery
feature.text:
You can regain some of your magical energy by studying your spell book. When you finish a Short Rest, you can choose expended spell slots to recover. The spell slots can have a combined level equal to no more than half your Wizard level (round up), and none of the slots can be level 6 or higher. For example, if you're a level 4 Wizard, you can recover up to two levels' worth of spell slots, regaining either one level 2 spell slot or two level 1 spell slots.
	Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 166

feature.name: Level 2: Scholar
feature.text:
While studying magic, you also specialized in another field of study. Choose one of the following skills in which you have proficiency: Arcana, History, Investigation, Medicine, Nature, or Religion. You have Expertise in the chosen skill.
Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 166

feature.name: Level 3: Wizard Subclass
feature.text:
You gain a Wizard subclass of your choice. The Abjurer, Diviner, Evoker, and Illusionist subclasses are detailed after this class's description. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Wizard levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Wizard level or lower.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 167

feature.name: Level 4: Ability Score Improvement
feature.text:
You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat (see chapter 5) or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Wizard levels 8, 12, and 16.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 167

feature.name: Level 5: Memorize Spell
feature.text:
Whenever you finish a Short Rest, you can study your spell book and replace one of the level 1+ Wizard spells you have prepared for your Spellcasting feature with another level 1+ spell from the book.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 167

feature.name: Level 8: Ability Score Improvement
feature.text:
You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat (see chapter 5) or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Wizard levels 8, 12, and 16.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 167

feature.name: Level 12: Ability Score Improvement
feature.text:
You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat (see chapter 5) or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Wizard levels 8, 12, and 16.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 167

feature.name: Level 16: Ability Score Improvement
feature.text:
You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat (see chapter 5) or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Wizard levels 8, 12, and 16.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 167

feature.name: Level 18: Spell Mastery
feature.text:
You have achieved such mastery over certain spells that you can cast them at will. Choose a level 1 and a level 2 spell in your spellbook that have a casting time of an action. You always have those spells prepared, and you can cast them at their lowest level without expending a spell slot. To cast either spell at a higher level, you must expend a spell slot.
	Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can study your spellbook and replace one of those spells with an eligible spell of the same level from the book.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 167

feature.name: Level 19: Epic Boon
feature.text:
You gain an Epic Boon feat (see chapter 5) or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Spell Recall is recommended.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 167

feature.name: Level 20: Signature Spells
feature.text:
Choose two level 3 spells in your spellbook as your signature spells. You always have these spells prepared, and you can cast each of them once at level 3 without expending a spell slot. When you do so, you can't cast them in this way again until you finish a Short or Long Rest. To cast either spell at a higher level, you must expend a spell slot.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 167

feature.name: Wizard Subclass: Abjurer
feature.text:
Shield Companions and Banish Foes

Your study of magic is focused on spells that block, banish, or protect-ending harmful effects, banishing evil influences, and protecting the weak. Abjurers are sought when baleful spirits require exorcism, when locations must be guarded against magical spying, and when portals to other planes of existence must be closed. Adventuring parties value Abjurers for the protection they provide against a variety of hostile magic and other attacks.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 172

feature.name: Level 3: Abjuration Savant (Abjurer)
feature.text:
Choose two Wizard spells from the Abjuration school, each of which must be no higher than level 2, and add them to your spellbook for free.
	In addition, whenever you gain access to a new level of spell slots in this class, you can add one Wizard spell from the Abjuration school to your spellbook for free. The chosen spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 172

feature.name: Level 3: Arcane Ward (Abjurer)
feature.text:
You can weave magic around yourself for protection. When you cast an Abjuration spell with a spell slot, you can simultaneously use a strand of the spell's magic to create a magical ward on yourself that lasts until you finish a Long Rest. The ward has a Hit Point maximum equal to twice your Wizard level plus your Intelligence modifier. Whenever you take damage, the ward takes the damage instead, and if you have any Resistances or Vulnerabilities, apply them before reducing the ward's Hit Points. If the damage reduces the ward to 0 hit points, you take any remaining damage. While the ward has 0 Hit Points, it can't absorb damage, but its magic remains.
	Whenever you cast an Abjuration spell with a spell slot, the ward regains a number of Hit Points equal to twice the level of the spell slot. Alternatively, as a Bonus Action, you can expend a spell slot, and the ward regains a number of Hit Points equal to twice the level of the spell slot expended.
	Once you create the ward, you can't create it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 172

feature.name: Level 6: Projected Ward (Abjurer)
feature.text:
When a creature that you can see within 30 feet of yourself takes damage, you can take a Reaction to cause your Arcane Ward to absorb that damage. If this damage reduces the ward to 0 Hit Points, the warded creature takes any remaining damage. If that creature has any Resistances or Vulnerabilities, apply them before reducing the ward's Hit Points.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 172

feature.name: Level 10: Spell Breaker (Abjurer)
feature.text:
You always have the Counterspell and Dispel Magic spells prepared. In addition, you can cast Dispel Magic as a Bonus Action, and you can add your Proficiency Bonus to its ability check.
	When you cast either spell with a spell slot, that slot isn't expended if the spell fails to stop a spell.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 172

feature.name: Level 14: Spell Resistance (Abjurer)
feature.text:
You have Advantage on saving throws against spells, and you have Resistance to the damage of spells.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 172

feature.name: Wizard Subclass: Diviner
feature.text:
Learn the Secrets of the Multi verse

The counsel of a Diviner is sought by those who want a clearer understanding of the past, present, and future. As a Diviner, you strive to part the veils of space, time, and consciousness. You work to master spells of discernment, remote viewing, supernatural knowledge, and foresight.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 173

feature.name: Level 3: Divination Savant (Diviner)
feature.text:
Choose two Wizard spells from the Divination school, each of which must be no higher than level 2, and add them to your spellbook for free.
	In addition, whenever you gain access to a new level of spell slots in this class, you can add one Wizard spell from the Divination school to your spellbook for free. The chosen spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 173

feature.name: Level 3: Portent (Diviner)
feature.text:
Glimpses of the future begin to press on your awareness. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, roll two d20s and record the numbers rolled. You can replace any D20 Test made by you or a creature that you can see with one of these foretelling rolls. You must choose to do so before the roll, and you can replace a roll in this way only once per turn.
	Each foretelling roll can be used only once. When you finish a Long Rest, you lose any unused foretelling rolls.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 173

feature.name: Level 6: Expert Divination (Diviner)
feature.text:
Casting Divination spells comes so easily to you that it expends only a fraction of your spellcasting efforts. When you cast a Divination spell using a level 2+ spell slot, you regain one expended spell slot. The slot you regain must be of a level lower than the slot you expended and can't be higher than level 5.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 173

feature.name: Level 10: The Third Eye (Diviner)
feature.text:
You can increase your powers of perception. As a Bonus Action, choose one of the following benefits, which lasts until you start a Short or Long Rest. You can't use this feature again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

	Darkvision. You gain Darkvision with a range of 120 feet.

	Greater Comprehension. You can read any language.

	See Invisibility. You can cast See Invisibility without expending a spell slot.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 173

feature.name: Level 14: Greater Portent (Diviner)
feature.text:
The visions in your dreams intensify and paint a more accurate picture in your mind of what is to come. Roll three d20s for your Portent feature rather than two.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 173

feature.name: Wizard Subclass: Evoker
feature.text:
Create Explosive Elemental Effects

Your studies focus on magic that creates powerful elemental effects such as bitter cold, searing flame, rolling thunder, crackling lightning, and burning acid. Some Evokers find employment in military forces, serving as artillery to blast armies from afar. Others use their power to protect others, while some seek their own gain.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 174

feature.name: Level 3: Evocation Savant (Evoker)
feature.text:
Choose two Wizard spells from the Evocation school, each of which must be no higher than level 2, and add them to your spellbook for free.
	In addition, whenever you gain access to a new level of spell slots in this class, you can add one Wizard spell from the Evocation school to your spellbook for free. The chosen spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 174

feature.name: Level 3: Potent Cantrip (Evoker)
feature.text:
Your damaging cantrips affect even creatures that avoid the brunt of the effect. When you cast a cantrip at a creature and you miss with the attack roll or the target succeeds on a saving throw against the cantrip, the target takes half the cantrip's damage (if any) but suffers no additional effect from the cantrip.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 174

feature.name: Level 6: Sculpt Spells (Evoker)
feature.text:
You can create pockets of relative safety within the effects of your evocations. When you cast an Evocation spell that affects other creatures that you can see, you can choose a number of them equal to 1 plus the spell's level. The chosen creatures automatically succeed on their saving throws against the spell, and they take no damage if they would normally take half damage on a successful save.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 174

feature.name: Level 10: Empowered Evocation (Evoker)
feature.text:
Whenever you cast a Wizard spell from the Evocation school, you can add your Intelligence modifier to one damage roll of that spell.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 174

feature.name: Level 14: Overchannel (Evoker)
feature.text:
You can increase the power of your spells. When you cast a Wizard spell with a spell slot of levels 1-5 that deals damage, you can deal maximum damage with that spell on the turn you cast it.
	The first time you do so, you suffer no adverse effect. If you use this feature again before you finish a Long Rest, you take 2d12 Necrotic damage for each level of the spell slot immediately after you cast it. This damage ignores Resistance and Immunity.
	Each time you use this feature again before finishing a Long Rest, the Necrotic damage per spell level increases by 1d12.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 174

feature.name: Wizard Subclass: Illusionist
feature.text:
Weave Subtle Spells of Deception

You specialize in magic that dazzles the senses and tricks the mind, and the illusions you craft make the impossible seem real.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 175

feature.name: Level 3: Illusion Savant (Illusionist)
feature.text:
Choose two Wizard spells from the Illusion school, each of which must be no higher than level 2, and add them to your spellbook for free.
	In addition, whenever you gain access to a new level of spell slots in this class, you can add one Wizard spell from the Illus ion school to your spellbook for free. The chosen spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 175

feature.name: Level 3: Improved Illusions (Illusionist)
feature.text:
You can cast Illusion spells without providing Verbal components, and if an Illusion spell you cast has a range of 10+ feet, the range increases by 60 feet.
	You also know the Minor Illusion cantrip. If you already know it, you learn a different Wizard cantrip of your choice. The cantrip doesn't count against your number of cantrips known. You can create both a sound and an image with a single casting of Minor Illusion, and you can cast it as a Bonus Action.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 175

feature.name: Level 6: Phantasmal Creatures (Illusionist)
feature.text:
You always have the Summon Beast and Summon Fey spells prepared. Whenever you cast either spell, you can change its school to Illusion, which causes the summoned creature to appear spectral. You can cast the Illusion version of each spell without expending a spell slot, but casting it without a slot halves the creature's Hit Points. Once you cast either spell without a spell slot, you must finish a Long Rest before you can cast the spell in that way again.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 175

feature.name: Level 10: Illusory Self (Illusionist)
feature.text:
When a creature hits you with an attack roll, you can take a Reaction to interpose an illusory duplicate of yourself between the attacker and yourself. The attack automatically misses you, then the illusion dissipates.
	Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 2+ spell slot (no action required).

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 175

feature.name: Level 14: Illusory Reality (Illusionist)
feature.text:
You have learned to weave shadow magic into your illusions to give them a semi-reality. When you cast an Illusion spell with a spell slot, you can choose one inanimate, nonmagical object that is part of the illusion and make that object real. You can do this on your turn as a Bonus Action while the spell is ongoing. The object remains real for 1 minute, during which it can't deal damage or give any conditions. For example, you can create an illusion of a bridge over a chasm and then make it real and cross it.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 175

feature.name: Wizard Subclass: Bladesinger
feature.text:
Wield Weapon and Wizardry in Elegant Tandem

Bladesingers master a tradition of wizardry that incorporates swordplay and dance. In combat, a Bladesinger uses intricate, elegant maneuvers that fend off harm and allow the Bladesinger to channel magic into devastating attacks and a cunning defense. Many who have observed a Bladesinger at work remember the display as one of the more beautiful experiences in their life—a glorious dance accompanied by a singing blade.
	Bladesinging is associated with the ancient elven societies that first mastered the art and coined the term. Even today, most Bladesingers still hail from old elven realms, such as Myth Drannor, or from non-elven societies that share land and history with elves, such as the Silver Marches. Wherever they hail from, Bladesingers take their talents all across the Realms to help common people and perform heroic deeds. Most communities greet the arrival of a Bladesinger as a good omen.

Source:	Forgotten Realms: Heroes of Faerûn [5.5e] p. 26

feature.name: Level 3: Bladesong (Bladesinger)
feature.text:
As a Bonus Action, you invoke an elven magic called the Bladesong, provided you aren't wearing armor or using a Shield.
	The Bladesong lasts for 1 minute and ends early if you have the Incapacitated condition, if you don armor or a Shield, or if you use two hands to make an attack with a weapon. You can dismiss the Bladesong at any time (no action required).
	While the Bladesong is active, you gain the following benefits. You can invoke the Bladesong a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest. You regain one expended use when you use Arcane Recovery.

	Agility. You gain a bonus to your AC equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of +1), and your Speed increases by 10 feet. In addition, you have Advantage on Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks.

	Bladework. Whenever you attack with a weapon with which you have proficiency, you can use your Intelligence modifier for the attack and damage rolls instead of using Strength or Dexterity.

	Focus. When you make a Constitution saving throw to maintain Concentration, you can add your Intelligence modifier to the total.

Source:	Forgotten Realms: Heroes of Faerûn [5.5e] p. 26

feature.name: Level 3: Training in War and Song (Bladesinger)
feature.text:
You gain proficiency with all Melee Martial weapons that don't have the Two-Handed or Heavy property. You can use a Melee weapon with which you have proficiency as a Spellcasting Focus for your Wizard spells.
	You also gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice: Acrobatics, Athletics, Performance, or Persuasion.

Source:	Forgotten Realms: Heroes of Faerûn [5.5e] p. 27

feature.name: Level 6: Extra Attack (Bladesinger)
feature.text:
You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn. Moreover, you can cast one of your Wizard cantrips that has a casting time of an action in place of one of those attacks.

Source:	Forgotten Realms: Heroes of Faerûn [5.5e] p. 27

feature.name: Level 10: Song of Defense (Bladesinger)
feature.text:
When you take damage while your Bladesong is active, you can take a Reaction to expend one spell slot and reduce the damage taken by an amount equal to five times the spell slot's level.

Source:	Forgotten Realms: Heroes of Faerûn [5.5e] p. 27

feature.name: Level 14: Song of Victory (Bladesinger)
feature.text:
After you cast a spell that has a casting time of an action, you can make one attack with a weapon as a Bonus Action.

Source:	Forgotten Realms: Heroes of Faerûn [5.5e] p. 27

feature.name: Level 3: Veilmark Information (Zamanora)
feature.text:
It is said that trespassing upon the spirit world leaves a tangible brand on one's body and soul. Mortals should never peer beyond the Veil, lest the spirits take notice and mark them forevermore. Let a marked person into your home and you invite certain calamity. The lands of Zamanora are riddled with such fiction and cautionary tales that only work to paint those who are inquisitive in a bad light. Yet they are right about one thing; someone who interacts with the Hidden World too often is bound to be "marked".

As characters engage in encounters with curses, spirits, and other supernatural phenomena, they accrue Veilmark. This attribute reflects their growing connection to the spirit realm and the transformative effects of these experiences on their physical and spiritual selves. Veilmarked is the term used by the Zamanori to describe individuals who have thus changed, and denotes characters who have accrued enough Veilmark to cross a threshold. If playing in a different setting, you may use the broader term Aura to describe the system.
	The influence of Veilmark on a character is determined by their Veilmark Score. The more a character interacts with curses, spirits, and other supernatural phenomena, delving into the mysteries of the Hidden World, the more their Veilmark Score increases. A character's Veilmark Score is effectively a pool of innate power they may tap into in order to produce certain effects that aid them when interacting with spiritual entities. However, at the same time, the higher one's Veilmark Score is, the more otherworldly they feel when interacting with their peers, making them wary and distrustful of their presence.
	Characters start out with a Veilmark Score of 0, which may increase up to a maximum of 100 throughout a campaign. Certain features, such as the Veilborn Origin (see Chapter II: Origins), or the Veilscarred Barbarian's Dark Bargain and Willow's Embrace (see Chapter II: Subclasses), signify that a character has already been extensively exposed to the Hidden World and influence that character's starting Veilmark Score according to their description.

Gaining Veilmark:
An increase of Veilmark results in noticeable physical changes, signifying the character's deepening connection with the spirit realm. Every time a character's Veilmark modifier increases, roll on the table below or choose one of the physical alterations listed to manifest on them.
	Your Veilmark Score may increase every time you experience an event that severely impacts your psyche by challenging what you priorly thought was real. Interacting with a being you believed to be a mere folktale, falling victim to a vicious curse, or drinking water from a bewitched spring can all increase your Veilmark Score. Such an experience, along with the implications caused upon oneself due to it, is known as a Harrow.
	A Harrow may affect a single or multiple characters at once, and at different levels of Severity (see Harrows table), based on roleplay and the narrative course of the story. For example, when a stranger who asks to share in the warmth of the party's campfire is later revealed to be a malign spirit, every character present may be subjected to a Harrow of Considerable level; yet for a character who recognizes the spirit as that of a deceased relative of theirs, the same Harrow may qualify as Intense. At the same time, another character who has already dabbled in occult practices to a point of communing with the spirits of the dead may treat this as a Harrow of Inconsequential level. The Severity of a Harrow on a character's psyche, as well as which character is subject to the risk of gaining Veilmark due to it and which isn't, is determined by the Storyteller, according to their interpretation of the player characters' backgrounds, stories, personalities, and any circumstantial factors that apply to each occasion.
	When the Storyteller declares a Harrow, each character that is subject to it must choose whether they wish to Resist or Embrace it. This choice represents their disposition towards the supernatural world, and their openness towards its truths and mysteries.

Reisting Veilmark:
A character who chooses to Resist a Harrow makes a Wisdom saving throw against a DC determined by its Severity. On a success, the experience leaves them unaffected, and nothing happens. On a failure, they must roll the corresponding Veilmark Die. Their Veilmark Score becomes increased by an amount equal to the result. A Hero that succeeds on their Action without Consequences resists the Harrow completely, taking no increase to their Veilmark Score. Otherwise, the Hero rolls the corresponding amount of Veilmark dice. A Success with Consequences means that the Hero's Veilmark increases by an amount equal to half of their result. A roll that only results in Consequences means that the Hero's Veilmark score is increased by the total amount rolled. You may also employ special means, such as the Veil Charm item (see Chapter IV: Fabled Relics), in order to better your chances in resisting any unwanted increases in your Veilmark Score.

Embracing Veilmark:
A character who chooses to Embrace a Harrow forgoes making any attempts at resisting its effects and does not roll the corresponding Veilmark Die. That character's Veilmark Score automatically increases by the maximum amount possible.

Veilmark:
d6 | Veilmark Die | DC | Status Tier
1 | 1d6 | 10 | harrowing-1
2 | 2d6 | 15 | harrowing-2
3 | 3d6 | 20 | harrowing-3
4 | 4d6 | 25 | harrowing-4
5 | 5d6 | 30 | harrowing-5

Veilmark Thresholds:
Whenever a Harrow causes your Veilmark Score to increase beyond the thresholds of 25, 50, 75 and 99 for the first time, you gain a Veilmark Transformation. For every Veilmark Transformation that you have, you gain a cumulative -2 penalty to any Influence Actions you take against other non-Veilmarked Humanoids and Beasts, unless you are trying to intimidate them.

Veilmark Thresholds Table:
Threshold | Title
25 | Shadowlit
50 | Equinoctial
75 | Moonstruck
99 | Spiritwalker

Transformations & Powers:
Veilmark transformations are a physical manifestation of the Hidden World's effects on your body. Such a transformation is a consequence of your innate understanding of the supernatural and ability to harness the powers that lie within, but ultimately comes at a cost. The first time you cross each of those Veilmark Thresholds, you gain a Veilmark Transformation and two new Veilmark Abilities from the tables below. For every Veilmark Transformation you have, you gain a cumulative -2 penalty to any Influence Actions you take against other non-Veilmarked Humanoids and Beasts, unless you are trying to intimidate them.

When you gain a new Veilmark Transformation, roll on the table below to determine its nature. If the result is a Transformation you have already undergone, roll again until you get a new one. Once you gain a Veilmark Transformation, it remains with you permanently, even if your Veilmark Score later decreases below that threshold.

Veilmark Transformations Table:
d10 | Transformation
1 | One of your eyes changes color. At night, when the Veil grows thin, you glimpse visions from the other side. This distraction grants you Disadvantage on Initiative rolls during nighttime hours.
2 | A streak of silver appears on your hair. Silvered weapons deal an extra Damage Die to you.
3 | Your skin's complexion becomes a tone paler. Whenever you take Fire damage you take an additional 1d4 Fire damage.
4 | Veins throughout your body become visibly dark beneath your skin. While you are Bloodied and can see an enemy, you can't willingly move away from them.
5 | Your shadow changes to resemble that of a different being. The Attitude of Beasts towards you worsens by one stage.
6 | A strange marking brands your skin like a scar. You have Disadvantage on saving throws made to resist the effects of Curses.
7 | A strange marking brands your skin like a scar. You have Disadvantage on saving throws made to resist the effects of Curses.
8 | A Zagovory symbol appears on your tongue. Whenever you fail an Influence Action, it is treated as attempted Intimidation regardless of your intentions.
9 | You appear sickly and weak. You have Disadvantage on saving throws made to resist the effects of Diseases.
10 | You no longer cast a reflection. You are excluded from beneficial effects caused by spells that target multiple creatures.

Every time you cross a Veilmark threshold, you unlock two new abilities, as detailed in the Veilmark Abilities table. You may use the abilities gained from each threshold a combined total of two times per day. For example, you may use one ability twice, or each ability once. Unlike Transformations, Veilmark Abilities do not last indefinitely. If your Veilmark Score falls below the Threshold that granted you these abilities (see Losing Veilmark), they become dormant and cannot be used until your Veilmark Score rises above the corresponding Threshold again.

Veilmark Threshold Abilities:

Shadowlit:

	Detect Spirit. You cast the spell Spirit Sense, without expending a spell slot.

	Incorporeal Reach. As a Bonus Action, your attacks harm the very essence of spirits for the next minute. For the duration, once per turn, you can deal an extra 1d6 Force damage to a target you hit with an attack or spell.

Equinoctial:

	Exorcism. As an Action, you touch a creature and end one of the following effects currently afflicting it: Frightened, Charmed, or a Possession.

	Pierce the Veil. As part of a successful Study Action made against a creature of the Spirit subtype, you discern either of the following: its Immunities, Resistances or Vulnerabilities.

Moonstruck:

	Soul Harvest. As a Reaction to a creature dying within 30 feet of you, you can infuse yourself with a fragment of its departing essence. As a result, you may choose to either regain a number of expended spell slots as a 4th-level Wizard using the Arcane Recovery feature, or gain 25 Temporary Hit Points.

	Spiritual Kinship. When you fail a saving throw against a spell or magical effect caused by a creature of the Spirit subtype, you succeed instead.

Spiritwalker:

	Ethereal Echo. As an Action, you create an ethereal duplicate of yourself that lasts for 1 minute. This spectral reflection appears in your space and mimics your movements precisely, with an almost imperceptible delay. The echo has half your current Hit Points. When you make an attack that deals damage to a single target, your echo repeats the attack but only deals half damage (rounded down). The echo takes the same damage as you do when you are damaged. It cannot regain Hit Points and vanishes if it reaches 0 Hit Points, you become Incapacitated, or when the duration ends.

	Tether Soul. By spending an hour in meditation, you bind your soul to a clearly defined point that you can see in your environment; for example, the hollow of an oak tree, or a statue made of stone. If you die before your next Long Rest, you gain the effects of the Reincarnate spell, but your new species is Haunt (see Chapter II: Species), while your new body forms in the bound point based on the materials it consists of. If you successfully return to life in this way, your Veilmark Score is reduced to 0 and you lose any Veilmark Transformations you have.

Losing Veilmark:
Once you have been exposed to the challenging truths of the Hidden World, it is very difficult, if indeed possible at all, to forget them. However, there are ways to reduce its impact on your being. The diminishing of one's Veilmark represents a retreat from the otherworldly, a return to the mundane, and a fixated anchoring to the Real. Below are the ways you may employ to reduce your Veilmark Score.

Downtime Activity:
You may choose to detach yourself from the supernatural by indulging in mundane activities for extended periods. For every month or Sojourn you spend this way, your Veilmark Score decreases by 5. Examples of such activities include:

	• Engaging with a community in manual labor, such as aiding in the building of a home.

	• Exploring and cultivating deep emotional bonds with others through steady everyday life.

	• Spending time alone to reflect upon yourself, or pursue artistic creations.

Recreation:
Other than spending time in peace and tranquility, you may also pursue more radical methods to reduce your Veilmark Score. These include consuming a God Flesh mushroom (see Chapter IV: Zamanoran Mushrooms), meditating within the Gemstone Caverns, or bathing in the waters of a lake within the Three Nines Forest. While such methods are the swiftest and most potent ways to achieve the intended result, they may carry certain hazards and must be undertaken with caution.

Potent Arcana:
Employing powerful magic, such as an archmage's spell of wishing, or returning to life through use of a Tether Soul (see Veilmark Abilities above) can reduce your Veilmark Score to 0, as well as remove any Veilmark Transformations you have. Once you surpass a Veilmark Threshold and gain a Veilmark Transformation, it remains with you permanently, even if your Veilmark Score later decreases below that threshold. Only Potent Arcana may remove a Veilmark Transformation. These transformations continue to affect both your body and soul, even if you disguise yourself through the means of illusory magic or a shape-changing ability. However, if your score increases again past a threshold you've previously crossed, you won't gain additional transformations for that same threshold. During a campaign in which you want to make the Veilmark system less punishing, you may rule that the effects of Greater Restoration also remove the effects of a Veilmark Transformation from a character. Conversely, reducing your Veilmark below each Threshold means that you lose access to the corresponding Abilities, as detailed above.

Roleplaying Veilmark:
As your Veilmark increases, consider how these changes affect your character's personality and demeanor. Do you welcome them as a mark of growth, or do you view them as aberrations upon your appearance? Consider how your personality might change to reflect them. You might become more aloof, skittish, or stoic. You may pick up a repetitive habit or mannerism. Perhaps the weight of the spirit world will deeply affect your psyche, gradually changing you into an altogether different person.

Social Implications:
In small communities such as the villages of Zamanora, these physical changes can lead to fear, reverence, or superstition. Characters bearing those marks are considered branded by the spirits, influencing their interactions with NPCs.

Fear and Distrust:
In most organized communities, the appearance of a Veilmarked stranger is met with apprehension, the locals fearing the character and associating their marks with bad omens or curses. Otherworldly features in their appearance might put the common folk ill at ease, but beyond that, their mere presence is unsettling for reasons that cannot be interpreted directly, as they carry the stigma of the Hidden World. A character with more than a couple of Veilmark transformations is usually treated as a Spook by common folk who first encounter them. Superstitious folk may be wary of such characters and treat them with extreme caution, to the point of turning them into a pariah amongst their societies or even chasing them away.

Reverence and Respect:
In the dwellings of spirits, or places where their presence is strongly felt, denizens might see the marks as a sign of a blessed or powerful individual, offering assistance or seeking their aid. In such cases, according to the Storyteller's discretion, the penalties to Influence Actions normally associated with Veilmark Transformations may become bonuses instead.

Source:	Zamanora: Ballad of the Witch p. 120 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Wizard Subclass: Oneiromancy (HB)
feature.text:
Oneiromancers are individuals that derive meaning from dreams, sought after for their precious counseling and guidance through life's many crucibles. The power of this ancient craft extends beyond the ability to foretell one's fate; powerful Oneiromancers can traverse the boundaries of the dreamscape, bringing forth lucid dreams and dreadful nightmares into the waking world.

Source:	Zamanora: Ballad of the Witch p. 114 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Oneirocritica (Oneiromancy (HB))
feature.text:
You can interpret the meaning behind your dreams and divulge prophetic signs for your imminent future. At the end of a Long Rest, roll a d10 on the Oneirocritica Signs table presented below. The result indicates the interpretation of your most recent dream. This interpretation grants you a benefit that will aid you throughout the day and lasts until you complete a Long Rest.

Oneirocritica Signs:
d10 | Interpretation | Effect
1 | You will meet the challenges ahead prepared | You have Advantage on your Initiative checks
2 | You will discover a hidden talent of yours | You gain proficiency on a skill of your choice
3 | You will find clarity in a troubling situation | When you fail a saving throw, you may reroll the die once and you must use the new roll
4 | Fortune favors you | When you roll a 1 on the d20, you may treat it as a 10
5 | The gods watch over you | You gain a bonus to your AC equal to half your Proficiency Bonus
6 | The road ahead is woeful, but you will persevere | You gain Resistance to one damage type of your choice
7 | Your health may take a turn for the worse | You gain Temporary Hit Points equal to twice your level
8 | Keep your loved ones close, or tragedy will befall you | While within 5 feet of an ally, you gain Immunity to the Frightened condition
9 | You must outrun the darkness, lest it consumes you | Your Speed increases by 10 feet
10 | Your hard work will pass unnoticed | Whenever you roll a 1 on a d20 Test, you have Advantage on your next d20 Test

When you reach level 6, you grow capable of discerning the ominous signs that are hidden in the dreams of others. Upon finishing a Long Rest, you can interpret the dreams of a number of willing creatures up to your Proficiency Bonus that have also finished a Long Rest within 30 feet of you, including yourself. Each of these creatures then rolls a d10 on the Oneirocritica Signs table and gains the corresponding benefit for the day.

Source:	Zamanora: Ballad of the Witch p. 114 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Hypnopedia (Oneiromancy (HB))
feature.text:
Choose one Wizard spell from the Divination school or Illusion school, which is no higher than level 2, and add it to your spellbook for free. In addition, whenever you gain access to a new level of spell slots in this class, you can add one Wizard spell from the Divination or the Illusion school to your spellbook for free. The chosen spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you may replace a spell learned this way with another Divination or Illusion spell of the same level.

Source:	Zamanora: Ballad of the Witch p. 115 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 6: Blissful Reverie (Oneiromancy (HB))
feature.text:
You may touch a willing creature at the beginning of its Short Rest and induce it with pleasant dreams. The creature falls asleep in a hypnotized state of elation for the duration of its rest. Upon finishing a Short Rest in this way, a creature gains the following benefits:

	Dreamlike Recovery. If the creature has the Spellcasting feature, it gains the effects of your Arcane Recovery feature (according to your Wizard level).

	Well Rested. If the creature spends Hit Dice for the purpose of regaining Hit Points, it forgoes rolling them and regains the maximum amount instead.

Once you have used this feature once, you cannot use it again until you roll a 1 to 5 on the Oneirocritica Signs table.

Source:	Zamanora: Ballad of the Witch p. 115 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 10: Waking Nightmare (Oneiromancy (HB))
feature.text:
You learn how to weave an apparition of your own nightmares and unleash it into the world. By using a Magic Action, you can cause a horrific illusion to appear in an unoccupied space within 15 feet of you. The illusion must resemble a creature and its size can be no larger than Large. The illusion includes sound, temperature, and other stimuli. It is active for the next minute or until you fall Unconscious. This feature has no effect on Undead or Constructs.
	At the end of each of your turns after the illusion appears, each creature within 5 feet of it makes a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC, suffering the effects of Phantasmal Killer on a failed save. While the illusion is active, you can use a Bonus Action on your turn to move it up to 20 feet.
	A creature rationalizes any illogical outcomes from interacting with the illusion, but it can use its Action to disbelieve it with an Intelligence (Investigation) check against your spell save DC. If the check succeeds, the creature realizes that the illusion is not real. The illusion then dissipates for the creature and any effects caused by it end on itself, yet every other creature in the area that has not succeeded on the same check can still perceive it.
	Once you have used this feature once, you cannot use it again until you roll a 6 to 10 on the Oneirocritica Signs table.

Source:	Zamanora: Ballad of the Witch p. 116 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 14: Gates of the Dreamworld (Oneiromancy (HB))
feature.text:
You are perpetually torn between the material world and the world of dreams, while your mind adapts into a state of constant awareness which manifests into reality. While you have the Unconscious condition, you may project a lucid apparition of yourself that hovers 5-feet over you. The apparition is intangible and cannot be interacted with.
	While the apparition is active, you can perceive your surroundings as if you were conscious. In addition, you can cast spells and use your Oneiromancer features normally, though they originate from the apparition. Spells that have a range of Self still target your physical form. You cannot cast spells that require material components in this way. The apparition dissipates as soon as you regain consciousness or die. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 5 spell slot or higher (no action required).

Source:	Zamanora: Ballad of the Witch p. 116 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Wizard Subclass: Soul Tethering (HB)
feature.text:
New mages uncover the secrets of the School of Soul Tethering out of their own volition. Instead, this powerful magic is usually the result of an arcane breakthrough due to a profoundly painful experience. Catalyzed by the tragic loss of a loved one, in a moment consumed by grief its practitioners turn to Necromancy, in a desperate bid to reverse the event. Though this is usually futile, in lands teeming with magic and spiritual tethers, where the ethereal realm is just beyond one's grasp, such a feat is possible. Once a spellcaster taps into these powers, they develop an innate ability to harness them.

Source:	Zamanora: Ballad of the Witch p. 117 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Progeny of Woe (Soul Tethering (HB))
feature.text:
You add the Find Familiar spell to your spellbook if it is not there already. Unlike a normal casting of the ritual, your casting is fueled by great loss, tethering the soul of a loved one. The familiar produced in this way, takes on an animal form that best befits the character of the lost loved one, retaining their personality and alignment. Once cast at least one time, even if the familiar dies the tether is not broken, and it can be brought back simply by casting the spell again.
	A soul tethered in this way can be targeted with Resurrection and does not require its original dead body in order to be brought back.

Source:	Zamanora: Ballad of the Witch p. 118 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Animancy (Soul Tethering (HB))
feature.text:
You learn how to tap into the magical energies of the spiritual realm. When you cast a Wizard spell, you can temporarily replace its damage type with Necrotic. When doing so, you can additionally choose to infuse the spell with fragments of your own soul, empowering it. If you do, you take Necrotic damage equal to twice the level of the spell, which can't be reduced in any way, and the spell deals 1 additional point of damage per die rolled. If a miss or a successful saving throw would prevent a spell empowered in this way from dealing damage, it deals half damage instead.
	You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	Zamanora: Ballad of the Witch p. 118 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 6: Memories of You (Soul Tethering (HB))
feature.text:
Your mastery over harnessing and manipulating the soul, allows you to create a temporary echo of a lost loved one. As a Magic Action, you can summon a Spiritual Anamnesis in an unoccupied space of your choice that you can see within 30 feet of you. The creature uses the Spiritual Anamnesis stat block and uses your Proficiency Bonus (PB). It gains the calling of a Caster, Expert or Warrior depending on the lost loved one's personality and talents, gaining various abilities.

	Combat. The Spiritual Anamnesis is an ally to you and your allies. In combat, it shares your Initiative count but if you have the Incapacitated condition, the spirit takes its turn immediately after yours and acts independently, focusing on protecting you. It can move and use its Reaction on its own, but the only Action it takes on its turn is the Dodge Action, unless you take a Bonus Action on your turn to command it to take another Action. That Action can be one in its stat block or some other Action. If you are Incapacitated, the spirit can take any Action of its choice, not just Dodge.

	Disappearance of the Anamnesis. The Spiritual Anamnesis persists for 1 hour, until it is reduced to 0 Hit Points, or until you die.

Once you awaken a Spiritual Anamnesis using this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest, unless you expend a spell slot of 3rd level or higher to use this feature again. You can only summon one spirit called by this feature at a time. If you use this feature and already have a spirit active, the first one immediately disappears.

Source:	Zamanora: Ballad of the Witch p. 118 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 10: Ties that Bind (Soul Tethering (HB))
feature.text:
Your abilities to call forth spirits increase and bind with them is strengthened. A spirit created through your Memories of You feature now lasts indefinitely, ending only if it is reduced to 0 Hit Points, or until you die. In addition, while within 30 feet of your Spiritual Anamnesis you may choose to gain Resistance to all damage as a Reaction to an attack, spell or ability. If you do, the spirit takes the same amount of damage as you did from that instance. Finally, a summoned Spiritual Anamnesis now retains more of its memories, gaining the following abilities depending on its calling:

	Caster. You can use your Reaction to transfer your Concentration over a spell to the Spiritual Anamnesis. As long as the spirit concentrates on a spell, it cannot use any other Action. By using a Bonus Action, you may reclaim Concentration over a spell from your spirit.

	Expert. The Spiritual Anamnesis can make ability checks using your spellcasting modifier instead of its own, glimpsing some memories of its long-lost expertise.

	Warrior. The Spiritual Anamnesis' Hit Points increase by a number equal to twice your Wizard level plus your Intelligence modifier.

Source:	Zamanora: Ballad of the Witch p. 118 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 14: Crescendo of Loss (Soul Tethering (HB))
feature.text:
Your mastery over influencing the souls of the lost has reached impossible heights, allowing you to tug at the souls of loved ones and summon them to your aid. As a Magic Action, you may summon the spirits of lost allies and friends to flit around you to a distance of 30 feet for 1 minute. As creatures exert themselves in the vicinity their souls fragment, magnetized by the apparitions you have brought forth. Creatures of your choice that take an Action or Reaction inside this area must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature takes 5d8 Necrotic damage, while you and Undead creatures of your choice in the area regain half as many Hit Points. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage.
	Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest. You can also restore its use of it by expending a level 5 spell slot or higher (no action required).

Source:	Zamanora: Ballad of the Witch p. 119 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Wizard Subclass: School of Circean Enchantment (HB)
feature.text:
Enthrall the others with charming magic

"And I will tell you of all the wicked witchcraft that Circe will try to practice upon you. She will mix a mess for you to drink, and she will drug the meal with which she makes it"
— Homer, Odyssey X

Theme: Inspired by the sorceress Circe from The Odyssey, this subclass focuses on enchanting, transforming, and manipulating others, blending charm and transmutation magic.

Playstyle: Circean Enchanters are masters of control, turning enemies into allies and reshaping their forms.

Circe is known for her role in Homer's Odyssey when Odysseus visits her island of Aeaea on the way back from the Trojan War. Circe had a vast knowledge of potions and herbs. Through the use of these and a magic wand or staff, she transformed her enemies, or those who offended her, into animals.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 67 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Enchanting Voice (School of Circean Enchantment (HB))
feature.text:
You learn the Charm Person spell and you can cast it without expending a spell slot once per Long Rest. When you cast the Charm Person spell, you can target an additional creature.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 67 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Will of the Sorceress (School of Circean Enchantment (HB))
feature.text:
When you cast a spell of the enchantment school that targets a creature, you can force that creature to have Disadvantage on the saving throw.
	Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 67 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 6: Transmutation's Touch (School of Circean Enchantment (HB))
feature.text:
You learn the Polymorph spell, but it doesn't count against your spells prepared.
	You can cast it once without expending a spell slot once per Long Rest.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 67 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 10: Beguile and Transform (School of Circean Enchantment (HB))
feature.text:
Your spells ignore Immunity to the Charmed condition. Your spells can also change the shape of creatures whose form is usually immutable, such as Constructs.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 67 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 14: Circe's Dominion (School of Circean Enchantment (HB))
feature.text:
As a Magic Action, you target a creature you can see within 30 feet of you. The creature must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failure, the creature is transformed into a harmless beast (CR 0) for to 1 minute. The creature retains its alignment and personality but is unable to act against you.
	Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 67 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Wizard Subclass: School of Illuminism (HB)
feature.text:
Bring the light of knowledge in the darkness

"Education is bitter, but its fruit is sweet"

Theme: Inspired by the Enlightenment, this subclass reflects a pursuit of knowledge, logic, and understanding of the natural world, using magic to illuminate both metaphorically and literally.

Playstyle: Illuminists excel at uncovering secrets, countering lies, and shedding light on mysteries. They have abilities that disrupt illusions, reveal hidden truths, and empower their allies with clarity.

The Enlightenment was an intellectual and philosophical movement taking place in Europe from the late 17th century to the early 19th century. The central doctrines of the Enlightenment were individual liberty, representative government, the rule of law, and religious freedom, in contrast to an absolute monarchy or single party state and the religious persecution of faiths other than those formally established and often controlled outright by the State.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 68 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Light of Truth (School of Illuminism (HB))
feature.text:
You learn the Detect Magic and Identify spells, which don't count against your spells prepared. You can cast each of these once without expending a spell slot, regaining the feature when you finish a Short or Long rest.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 68 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Dispel the Shadows (School of Illuminism (HB))
feature.text:
When you cast a spell that creates light (such as Light or Daylight), the radius of the light is doubled.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 68 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 6: Unveiling Insight (School of Illuminism (HB))
feature.text:
You gain Advantage on Intelligence (Investigation) and Wisdom (Insight) checks. Additionally, as a Magic Action, you can focus your mind to gain Truesight up to 30 feet for 1 minute.
	Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 68 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 10: Illuminated Mind (School of Illuminism (HB))
feature.text:
Your mind resists magical manipulation. You are Immune to the Charmed condition.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 68 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 14: Brilliant Revelation (School of Illuminism (HB))
feature.text:
As a Magic Action, you emit a burst of magical light in a 30-foot radius. Creatures of your choice within the radius must make a Constitution saving throw against a spell save DC. Failure: Blinded condition for 1 minute. While Blinded, can't have the Invisible condition. An affected creature can make another Constitution saving throw at the end of each of its next turns, ending the condition on itself on a success.
	Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 68 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Wizard Subclass: School of the Alchemist (HB)
feature.text:
Master of Transformation and Elixirs

"Every element holds a secret, every reaction a revelation. To seek the philosopher's stone is to seek the divine"

Theme: Rooted in medieval alchemical traditions, this subclass focuses on transmutation, creation, and the pursuit of perfection.

Playstyle: Alchemists are versatile, able to create potions, transmute materials, and alter the battlefield.

The School of Alchemy is a discipline of arcane science, blending mystical knowledge with chemistry, metallurgy, and the natural philosophy of medieval and Renaissance Europe. These wizards embody the historical alchemists who sought the Philosopher's Stone, dabbled in transmutation, and believed that magic and science were two sides of the same coin. Rooted in the traditions of figures like Paracelsus, Albertus Magnus, and Nicolas Flamel, this school explores the alchemical mysteries of matter, energy, and spiritual transformation.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 66 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Transmutation Magic (School of the Alchemist (HB))
feature.text:
You learn the Alter Self spell, which doesn't count against your spells prepared. You can cast it once without expending a spell slot, once per Long Rest.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 66 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Alchemical Recipes (School of the Alchemist (HB))
feature.text:
During a Long Rest, you can create a potion. Choose from the following: healing, resistance (to one damage type), or speed (increases movement by 10 feet for 1 hour). The DM has the statistics for the potions.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 66 (Homebrew)
